q: An amount is due to a zonal railway from an outside party, while another amount is due by the railway to a supplier. Which of the following correctly distinguishes the heads 'Demands Recoverable' and 'Demands Payable' under which such amounts are held?

options.A: Amounts due to the Railways are credited to Demands Recoverable, whereas amounts due by the Railways are debited to Demands Payable
options.B: Both heads record amounts due to the Railways from outside parties
options.C: Amounts due to the Railways from outside parties for services rendered, pending realisation, are debited to Demands Recoverable, whereas amounts due by the Railways to outside parties for goods and services received, pending payment, are credited to Demands Payable
options.D: Demands Recoverable relates to transactions with other railways, whereas Demands Payable relates to transactions with the Railway Board

e: Amounts due to the Railways from outside parties, pending realisation, are debited to Demands Recoverable, while amounts due by the Railways for goods and services received, pending payment, are credited to Demands Payable.

q: A clerk proposes to finance a passenger amenity work from the Capital Fund and an asset-creating work from the Development Fund. Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Capital Fund from the Development Fund of the Railways?

options.A: The Capital Fund is used for passenger amenities and labour welfare works, whereas the Development Fund is used for financing asset-creating capital works
options.B: The Capital Fund is credited with the safety surcharge on passenger fares, whereas the Development Fund is credited out of the surplus
options.C: Both the funds can be used only for renewal and replacement of existing assets
options.D: The Capital Fund is used mainly for financing asset-creating (capital) works out of the Railways' internal resources, whereas the Development Fund is used for works relating to passenger amenities, labour welfare and operational improvements, which may not be directly remunerative

e: The Capital Fund finances asset-creating capital works out of internal resources, while the Development Fund finances passenger amenities, labour welfare and operational improvement works that may not be directly remunerative.

q: In the Pink Book, some works are listed one by one while other similar small works are grouped together under a single provision. Which of the following correctly distinguishes such 'itemised works' from an 'umbrella work'?

options.A: Itemised works are groups of similar small works provided with a lumpsum provision, whereas an umbrella work is a single work shown individually
options.B: Works costing more than the prescribed limit are shown individually as itemised works, whereas an umbrella work is a group of similar small works provided for together with a lumpsum provision under one head
options.C: Both itemised works and umbrella works are shown individually in the Pink Book
options.D: Itemised works require the sanction of the Railway Board, whereas umbrella works require no sanction at all

e: Works above the prescribed limit are shown individually in the Pink Book as itemised works, while an umbrella work groups similar small works together with one lumpsum provision.

q: An audit party has to verify that the moneys disbursed by a zonal railway were legally available for, and were applied to, the services and purposes for which Parliament made the grants and appropriations. This kind of audit, conducted on behalf of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India, is known as:

options.A: Appropriation audit
options.B: Performance audit
options.C: Propriety audit
options.D: Efficiency audit

e: Appropriation audit verifies that moneys disbursed were legally available for, and were applied to, the services and purposes for which Parliament made the grants and appropriations.

q: For a service of great magnitude whose details cannot be stated in advance in a Demand for Grant, Parliament makes a grant under Article 116 of the Constitution which is often described as a 'blank cheque' to the Government, because the demand cannot be stated with the details ordinarily given in a Demand for Grant. Such a grant is a:

options.A: Vote on Account
options.B: Exceptional Grant
options.C: Vote of Credit
options.D: Token Grant

e: A Vote of Credit under Article 116 is a grant for a service of great magnitude whose details cannot be stated in advance; it is like a blank cheque, unlike a Vote on Account or an Exceptional Grant.

q: A zonal railway is preparing a note on the financing pattern of the Rashtriya Rail Sanraksha Kosh, which assures an annual outlay of Rs 20,000 crore for safety works. Of this assured annual outlay, the share borne by Gross Budgetary Support is:

options.A: Rs 15,000 crore
options.B: Rs 5,000 crore
options.C: Rs 10,000 crore
options.D: Rs 20,000 crore

e: The RRSK assures Rs 20,000 crore a year for safety works, of which Rs 15,000 crore is borne by Gross Budgetary Support and the balance of Rs 5,000 crore from the Railways' internal resources.

q: To build up the corpus of the Special Railway Safety Fund (SRSF), the Railways themselves contributed about Rs 5,000 crore. This contribution of the Railways was raised mainly through:

options.A: Market borrowings raised by the Indian Railway Finance Corporation
options.B: A safety surcharge levied on passenger fares
options.C: Appropriations from the Railway Pension Fund
options.D: Sale of surplus railway land

e: Towards the SRSF corpus of Rs 17,000 crore, the Railways' own contribution of about Rs 5,000 crore was raised mainly through the safety surcharge levied on passenger fares.

q: The Special Railway Safety Fund (SRSF) was wound up in the year 2008. On its closure, the unspent balance lying in the Fund was transferred to:

options.A: The Capital Fund of the Railways
options.B: The Railway Safety Fund
options.C: The Depreciation Reserve Fund of the Railways
options.D: The general revenues of the Government of India

e: The Special Railway Safety Fund was wound up in 2008 on completion of its term, and its unspent balance was transferred to the Depreciation Reserve Fund of the Railways.

q: A clerk has to state where the balances accumulated in the National Small Savings Fund, which holds the collections under the small savings schemes, are deployed. These balances are invested in:

options.A: Equity shares of public sector undertakings
options.B: Treasury Bills only
options.C: Loans and advances to railway public sector undertakings
options.D: Central and State Government securities

e: The balances of the National Small Savings Fund are invested in Central and State Government securities, so that the small savings collections finance Government borrowing.

q: For exhibiting the accounts of the Government of India in their three parts, a clerk places the Public Account of India in Part I along with the Consolidated Fund. The Public Account of India correctly forms:

options.A: Part III of the Government accounts
options.B: Part I of the Government accounts
options.C: Part II of the Government accounts
options.D: A section of the Consolidated Fund of India

e: Government accounts are exhibited in three parts: Part I the Consolidated Fund, Part II the Contingency Fund and Part III the Public Account of India, so the Public Account belongs to Part III.

q: A Member of Parliament, new to the Budget papers, wants a single document which will explain to him the other Budget documents and the technical terms used in them. The document meant for this purpose is the:

options.A: Budget at a Glance
options.B: Key to Budget Documents
options.C: Detailed Demands for Grants
options.D: Expenditure Profile

e: The Key to Budget Documents is the single Budget document that explains the other Budget documents and the technical terms used in them, for the guidance of readers such as new Members of Parliament.

q: A Bill is proposed to be certified as a Money Bill, but one of its provisions relates to a subject outside Article 110 of the Constitution. Which of the following subjects cannot be dealt with in a Money Bill?

options.A: The imposition, abolition or alteration of any tax
options.B: The appropriation of moneys out of the Consolidated Fund of India
options.C: The creation of an All-India Service
options.D: Declaring any expenditure to be expenditure charged on the Consolidated Fund of India

e: A Money Bill under Article 110 can deal only with the listed fiscal subjects such as taxation, borrowing and appropriation; creation of an All-India Service is outside Article 110 and cannot be in a Money Bill.

q: Among the statements laid before Parliament under the FRBM Act, the one which sets out three-year rolling targets for the specified fiscal indicators is the:

options.A: Macro-Economic Framework Statement
options.B: Fiscal Policy Strategy Statement
options.C: Medium-Term Expenditure Framework Statement
options.D: Medium-Term Fiscal Policy Statement

e: Of the FRBM statements, the Medium-Term Fiscal Policy Statement sets out three-year rolling targets for the specified fiscal indicators such as fiscal deficit and revenue deficit.

q: Before 1 April 1997, temporary mismatches in the cash flow of the Central Government were met through ad hoc Treasury Bills. The system which replaced the ad hoc Treasury Bills with effect from that date is the system of:

options.A: Cash Management Bills
options.B: Ways and Means Advances
options.C: Dated Government securities
options.D: Market Stabilisation Scheme

e: Ad hoc Treasury Bills were discontinued from 1 April 1997 and replaced by Ways and Means Advances from the Reserve Bank, for meeting temporary cash flow mismatches of the Central Government.

q: The Railway Convention Committee, which reviews the financial relationship between the Railways and General Finances, was first constituted after Independence in the year:
e: The Railway Convention Committee, which periodically reviews the financial relationship between the Railways and General Finances, was first constituted after Independence in 1949.

q: A doubt is raised as to how the Railway Convention Committee, an ad hoc Parliamentary committee, comes into existence. The Committee is constituted:

options.A: By the President under Article 263 of the Constitution
options.B: By the Railway Board through an office order
options.C: On a resolution adopted by the Lok Sabha and concurred in by the Rajya Sabha
options.D: By the Finance Commission along with its report

e: The Railway Convention Committee is an ad hoc Parliamentary committee constituted on a resolution adopted by the Lok Sabha and concurred in by the Rajya Sabha.

q: An item of expenditure has been booked under a wrong head of account, and an assistant fears that the Trial Balance of the railway will not agree on this account. The correct position is that such an error of classification:

options.A: Prevents the Trial Balance of the railway from agreeing
options.B: Is brought to light automatically by the Trial Balance
options.C: Can be rectified only with the sanction of the Railway Board
options.D: Does not affect the agreement of the Trial Balance, since the total debits and total credits remain equal

e: A wrong classification changes only which head is debited or credited, not the total debits and credits, so the Trial Balance still agrees and the error does not come to light through it.

q: For reconciling the transactions of the accredited bank with the railway books, the Accounts Office relies on the daily statement of receipts and payments rendered by the bank. This daily statement is known as the:

options.A: Bank Scroll
options.B: Account Current
options.C: Classified Abstract
options.D: Debt Head Report

e: The daily statement of receipts and payments rendered by the accredited bank for reconciliation with the railway books is known as the Bank Scroll.

q: In the Accounts Office of a zonal railway, a question arises whether the Registers of Earnings, the Revenue Allocation Registers, the Registers of Works and the Suspense Registers belong to the General Books. These registers are classified as:

options.A: General Books
options.B: Subsidiary records
options.C: Initial records of the executive departments
options.D: Registers of the Audit Department

e: The Registers of Earnings, Revenue Allocation Registers, Registers of Works and Suspense Registers are subsidiary records supporting the General Books, not General Books themselves.

q: The declared provisions of a Finance Bill relating to customs and excise duties take provisional effect on its introduction under a statute enacted long before Independence. That statute, the Provisional Collection of Taxes Act, was enacted in the year:
e: The Provisional Collection of Taxes Act, under which the declared customs and excise provisions of a Finance Bill take provisional effect on introduction, was enacted in 1931.

q: Advances are taken from the Contingency Fund of India to meet urgent unforeseen expenditure pending authorisation by Parliament. The Fund itself, established under Article 267 of the Constitution, is regulated by:

options.A: The General Financial Rules
options.B: The FRBM Act, 2003
options.C: The Appropriation Act of the year concerned
options.D: The Contingency Fund of India Act, 1950

e: The Contingency Fund of India, established under Article 267, is regulated by the Contingency Fund of India Act, 1950, which governs advances from it and their recoupment.

q: The Government of India receives the dividends declared by railway public sector undertakings such as IRCTC and IRFC. In the Union Government accounts, these dividends are classified as:

options.A: Capital receipts
options.B: Non-tax revenue receipts
options.C: Sundry Other Earnings of the Railways
options.D: Receipts under the Public Account of India

e: Dividends received by the Government from its undertakings, including railway PSUs such as IRCTC and IRFC, are non-tax revenue receipts in the Union Government accounts.

q: After the full Budget is voted, a clerk proposes to treat the amount earlier granted through the Vote on Account as an extra grant over and above the total grant for the year. The correct position is that the amount granted through a Vote on Account:

options.A: Forms part of the total grant for the year and is merged in it when the full grant is voted
options.B: Is in addition to the total grant voted for the year
options.C: Lapses if it is not spent within one month of the grant
options.D: Is expenditure charged on the Consolidated Fund of India

e: A Vote on Account is only an advance grant for part of the year; its amount forms part of, and is merged in, the total grant for the year when the full Budget is voted.

q: A Parliamentary committee which examines the estimates of the Ministries and reports what economies can be effected consists of thirty members drawn exclusively from one House. The Estimates Committee of Parliament consists of:

options.A: 22 members drawn from both Houses of Parliament
options.B: 15 members, all from the Rajya Sabha
options.C: 30 members, all from the Lok Sabha
options.D: 45 members drawn from both Houses of Parliament

e: The Estimates Committee, which examines the estimates of Ministries and suggests economies, consists of 30 members, all drawn from the Lok Sabha.

q: To meet a temporary mismatch in its cash flow, the Government of India issues Cash Management Bills, distinct from the regular Treasury Bills. The maturity period of such Cash Management Bills is:

options.A: Exactly 364 days
options.B: More than one year
options.C: Exactly 182 days
options.D: Less than 91 days

e: Cash Management Bills are issued for temporary cash mismatches with a maturity of less than 91 days, shorter than the regular 91, 182 and 364 day Treasury Bills.

q: A Station Master proposes to meet the contingent expenditure of his station out of the earnings collected at the station and to remit only the balance. The correct position is that the earnings collected at a station are required to be:

options.A: Remitted in full to the Cash Office or the accredited bank, and not utilised for local expenditure
options.B: Utilised for meeting the contingent expenditure of the station
options.C: Retained at the station till the close of the financial year
options.D: Adjusted against the imprest held by the Station Master

e: Station earnings must be remitted in full to the Cash Office or the accredited bank; they cannot be used for local contingent expenditure, which is met from the imprest or by bill.

q: While exhibiting the Special Railway Safety Fund in the Public Account of India, a clerk proposes to place it under Major Head 8009 along with the State Provident Funds. The Fund was correctly maintained under Major Head:
e: The Special Railway Safety Fund was maintained in the Public Account under Major Head 8230, with minor heads for its commercial and strategic portions, as per the List of Major and Minor Heads.

q: During the year, a Supplementary Demand for Grants of the Ministry of Railways is taken up directly for voting, without the stage of examination which the main Demands undergo. Unlike the main Demands for Grants presented with the Budget, the Supplementary Demands are:

options.A: Examined by the Public Accounts Committee before they are voted
options.B: Voted only by the Rajya Sabha
options.C: Voted by the Lok Sabha without prior examination by the Departmentally Related Standing Committees
options.D: Presented only during the Budget session of Parliament

e: Supplementary Demands for Grants are voted by the Lok Sabha during the year without the prior detailed examination by the Departmentally Related Standing Committees that the main Demands undergo.

q: In the Budget documents, the salaries and allowances of certain constitutional functionaries are shown as charged expenditure and are not voted. The salaries and allowances of the Speaker and the Deputy Speaker of the Lok Sabha are:

options.A: Submitted to the vote of the Lok Sabha every year
options.B: Met out of the Public Account of India
options.C: Paid out of the Contingency Fund of India
options.D: Charged on the Consolidated Fund of India

e: The salaries and allowances of the Speaker and the Deputy Speaker of the Lok Sabha are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India under Article 112(3) and are not submitted to vote.

q: A clerk proposes to show the pensions payable to the Judges of the Supreme Court as voted expenditure, on the ground that only their salaries are charged. The pensions payable to or in respect of the Judges of the Supreme Court of India are:

options.A: Submitted to the vote of Parliament every year
options.B: Charged on the Consolidated Fund of India
options.C: Charged on the Consolidated Funds of the States
options.D: Met out of the Public Account of India

e: Not only the salaries but also the pensions payable to or in respect of Supreme Court Judges are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India and are not voted by Parliament.

q: It is proposed to declare the expenditure on a service, not specified in the Constitution itself, as expenditure charged on the Consolidated Fund of India. Such a declaration can be made by:

options.A: Parliament by law
options.B: The President by an order
options.C: The Finance Minister by a notification
options.D: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India

e: Parliament may by law declare any other expenditure to be expenditure charged on the Consolidated Fund of India, as provided in Article 112(3); no executive order can do so.

q: During a financial year, the Ministry of Railways needs additional grants at more than one stage and presents Supplementary Demands accordingly. Supplementary Demands for Grants are ordinarily presented to Parliament during the course of a financial year in:

options.A: One batch only
options.B: Two batches
options.C: Three batches
options.D: Five batches

e: Supplementary Demands for Grants are ordinarily presented to Parliament in three batches during a financial year, in the monsoon, winter and the final batch with the Budget session.

q: In budgetary terminology, a Demand for Grant changes its name once the Lok Sabha has voted it. After it has been passed (voted) by the Lok Sabha, a Demand for Grant becomes:

options.A: An Appropriation
options.B: A Vote on Account
options.C: A Budget Allotment
options.D: A Grant

e: A Demand for Grant is the estimate in demand form; once the Lok Sabha votes it, it becomes a Grant, which the Appropriation Act then authorises for withdrawal.

q: In his Budget Speech, the Finance Minister first gives an overview of the economy and announces the major policies of the Government, and only thereafter comes to the taxation proposals. This overview portion of the Speech is its:

options.A: Part A
options.B: Part B
options.C: Annexure on the Demands for Grants
options.D: Explanatory Memorandum

e: Part A of the Budget Speech gives the overview of the economy and the major policies of the Government; the taxation proposals come later in Part B.

q:
A question arises in the Accounts Office about the Finance Commission constituted under Article 280 of the Constitution. Consider the following statements in this connection:
1. The Finance Commission is constituted by the President once in five years, or earlier if the President considers it necessary.
2. The Government of India is bound to implement the recommendations of the Finance Commission without any modification.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Under Article 280, the President constitutes the Finance Commission every five years or earlier if he considers it necessary; its recommendations are advisory and not binding as such, so only statement 1 is correct.

q:
Supplementary estimates relating to charged expenditure are also presented during the course of the year. Consider the following statements in this connection:
1. Such supplementary estimates for charged expenditure are presented to the Lok Sabha along with the Supplementary Demands for Grants.
2. Being charged expenditure, these estimates are not submitted to the vote of the Lok Sabha.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Supplementary estimates for charged expenditure are presented to the Lok Sabha along with the Supplementary Demands, but being charged expenditure they are discussed, not voted, so both statements are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Rajya Sabha may amend a Money Bill, and the Lok Sabha is bound to accept the amendments so made.
2. Article 109 of the Constitution lays down a special procedure for the passage of Money Bills in Parliament.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: The Rajya Sabha can only recommend amendments to a Money Bill, which the Lok Sabha may accept or reject; Article 109 lays down the special procedure for Money Bills, so only statement 2 is correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The balance under 'Manufacturing Suspense', representing the cost of jobs in progress in workshops, is exhibited in the Balance Sheet of the Railways as part of the working expenses of the year.
2. The debit balance under 'Stores Suspense' (Plan Head 71), representing the value of the stores held in stock in the depots, forms part of the Block Account of the Railways.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Manufacturing Suspense is an asset head for work-in-progress, not working expenses; the debit balance under Stores Suspense (Plan Head 71), being stores held in stock, forms part of the Block Account, so only statement 2 is correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Journal Vouchers and cash vouchers in the books of a railway are numbered in one common serial series.
2. A journal (transfer) entry in the books of a railway may be passed without a Journal Voucher duly signed by an Accounts Officer.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Journal Vouchers and cash vouchers run in separate serial series, and no journal or transfer entry can be passed without a Journal Voucher signed by an Accounts Officer, so both statements are wrong.

q:
A payee has not encashed a cheque issued by a zonal railway for a long time. Consider the following statements in this connection:
1. The cheque remains valid for payment for three months from the date of its issue.
2. After that period, the cheque is treated as time-barred and its amount is written back in the books through a transfer entry.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: A railway cheque is valid for payment for three months from its date; after that it is time-barred and its amount is written back in the books by a transfer entry, so both statements are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. 'Cash-in-Transit' in the railway books is cleared when a cheque is issued by the Cash & Pay Office.
2. 'Cash-in-Transit' is cleared when the amount remitted is credited by the bank and taken to account under 'Deposits with Reserve Bank'.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Cash-in-Transit is cleared only when the remitted amount is actually credited by the bank and taken to account under Deposits with Reserve Bank, not merely when a cheque is issued, so only statement 2 is correct.

q: Two Bills connected with the Budget — one giving effect to the taxation proposals and the other authorising withdrawals from the Consolidated Fund — are sometimes confused with each other. Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Finance Bill from the Appropriation Bill?

options.A: The Finance Bill authorises withdrawal of moneys from the Consolidated Fund of India, whereas the Appropriation Bill gives effect to the taxation proposals of the Budget
options.B: The Finance Bill is introduced after the Appropriation Act has been passed, whereas the Appropriation Bill is introduced along with the Budget
options.C: Both the Finance Bill and the Appropriation Bill authorise withdrawal of moneys from the Consolidated Fund of India
options.D: The Finance Bill gives effect to the financial (taxation) proposals of the Budget, whereas the Appropriation Bill authorises the withdrawal of moneys from the Consolidated Fund of India to meet the grants voted and the expenditure charged thereon

e: The Finance Bill gives effect to the taxation and other financial proposals of the Budget, while the Appropriation Bill authorises withdrawal of moneys from the Consolidated Fund to meet the voted grants and charged expenditure.

q: An Accounts Assistant, while operating the debt heads, confuses suspense heads with remittance heads. Which of the following correctly distinguishes the two?

options.A: Suspense heads record transactions which are held temporarily pending their clearance to the final heads of account, whereas remittance heads record transactions in the course of settlement between accounting units, such as moneys remitted from one unit to another
options.B: Suspense heads are operated only by the Railway Board, whereas remittance heads are operated only by the divisions
options.C: Suspense heads record cash in transit, whereas remittance heads record amounts awaiting classification
options.D: There is no difference between the two; both record transactions in the course of settlement

e: Suspense heads hold transactions temporarily pending clearance to their final heads of account, while remittance heads record transactions in course of settlement between accounting units, such as remittances from one unit to another.

q: In the terminology of the Railways' Works Programme, which of the following correctly distinguishes the 'outlay' on a work from its 'throw-forward'?

options.A: The outlay is the total sanctioned cost of the work, whereas the throw-forward is the expenditure already incurred on it
options.B: The outlay relates to works already completed, whereas the throw-forward relates to works not yet sanctioned
options.C: The outlay is provided by the Railway Board, whereas the throw-forward is provided by the zonal railway
options.D: The outlay is the amount provided for expenditure on the work during the year, whereas the throw-forward is the balance of the sanctioned cost which will remain to be incurred in the subsequent years

e: The outlay on a work is the amount provided for expenditure on it during the year, while the throw-forward is the balance of its sanctioned cost still to be incurred in the following years.

q: The management of a zonal railway works with two sets of earnings figures during a year — provisional figures compiled at short intervals and final figures brought to account. Which of the following correctly distinguishes 'approximate earnings' from 'accounted earnings'?

options.A: Approximate earnings relate to goods traffic only, whereas accounted earnings relate to coaching traffic only
options.B: Approximate earnings are compiled by the Railway Board, whereas accounted earnings are compiled by the stations
options.C: Approximate earnings are the provisional figures compiled at short intervals from the station returns, before internal check and apportionment, whereas accounted earnings are the final figures brought to account after check and apportionment, as compiled in the Traffic Book
options.D: Approximate earnings are the final audited figures, whereas accounted earnings are provisional figures

e: Approximate earnings are provisional figures compiled at short intervals from station returns before check and apportionment, while accounted earnings are the final figures brought to account in the Traffic Book after check and apportionment.

q: At the monthly review meeting of a zonal railway, the earnings and expenditure of the period are compared with the corresponding budget figures to watch the pace of working. The monthly financial review primarily compares the actual earnings and expenditure of the period with:

options.A: The actuals of the corresponding period of the previous year only
options.B: The Final Modification Estimates of the previous year
options.C: The estimates of the other zonal railways
options.D: The Budget Estimates and the proportionate allotment for the period

e: The monthly financial review watches progress by comparing the actual earnings and expenditure of the period with the Budget Estimates and the proportionate budget allotment for that period.

q: Along with the Appropriation Accounts of the Railways, an account dealing with the differences in the value and quantity of stores is furnished as an annexure. That annexure is the:

options.A: The Stock Adjustment Account
options.B: The Trial Balance
options.C: The Pink Book statement of works
options.D: The Suspense Register

e: The Stock Adjustment Account, furnished as an annexure to the Appropriation Accounts, deals with differences between the priced and physical values and quantities of stores.

q: Savings are available under one work and an excess is foreseen under another work, both the works falling under the same Plan Head and the same grant. Such a re-appropriation of funds between the two works can be sanctioned by:

options.A: The Railway Board only
options.B: The General Manager of the zonal railway, with the concurrence of the associated finance
options.C: The Divisional Railway Manager alone
options.D: The Principal Financial Adviser alone

e: Re-appropriation between works under the same Plan Head and the same grant can be sanctioned by the General Manager of the zonal railway, with the concurrence of the associated finance.

q: One zonal railway raises a debit against another railway through a Transfer Certificate, but the respondent railway finds the debit raised against it unacceptable. The correct course for the respondent railway is to:

options.A: Pay the amount immediately and claim a refund later
options.B: Write off the amount with the sanction of its General Manager
options.C: Return the Transfer Certificate with its objections, the item remaining outstanding till the matter is settled
options.D: Charge the amount to its ordinary working expenses

e: A respondent railway that finds a debit raised by Transfer Certificate unacceptable returns the Transfer Certificate with its objections, and the item stays outstanding till the matter is settled between the railways.

q: At the close of a day, certain PRS/UTS earnings stand transferred electronically by the accredited bank but have not yet been credited to the Railways' account. In the railway accounts, these earnings are shown as:

options.A: Sundry Other Earnings
options.B: A credit balance under Traffic Suspense
options.C: Deposits with Reserve Bank
options.D: Cash-in-Transit

e: PRS/UTS earnings transferred electronically by the bank but not yet credited to the Railways' account are in transit at the day's close and are therefore shown as Cash-in-Transit under the remittance heads.

q:
Consider the following statements about the sub-divisions of Major Head 5002 in the Government accounts:
1. Sub-Major Head 01 under Major Head 5002 represents capital bearing dividend liability.
2. Sub-Major Head 02 under Major Head 5002 represents capital free of dividend liability.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: In the classification under Major Head 5002, Capital Outlay on Railways, Sub-Major Head 01 covers capital bearing dividend liability and Sub-Major Head 02 covers capital free of dividend liability, so both statements are correct.

q: An Accounts Assistant, after closing the Journal Book and the Classified Abstract for a month, has to make the postings in the Ledger of the railway. These postings are made from:

options.A: The Station Balance Sheets rendered by the stations
options.B: The bank scrolls received from the accredited bank
options.C: The Works Registers maintained in the Accounts Office
options.D: The closing totals of the Journal and the Classified Abstract

e: Ledger postings in railway accounts are made from the closing totals of the Journal Book and the Classified Abstract, which summarise the month's transactions head-wise after the subsidiary books are closed.

q: A question is raised whether the administrative expenses of the office of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India, including the salaries of the Comptroller and Auditor General and of the persons serving in that office, are voted by Parliament every year. The correct position is that such expenses are:

options.A: Charged on the Consolidated Fund of India
options.B: Submitted to the vote of Parliament every year
options.C: Met out of the Contingency Fund of India
options.D: Shared equally between the Union and the States

e: Article 148(6) of the Constitution provides that the administrative expenses of the CAG's office, including salaries of the CAG and his staff, are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India and are not voted annually.

q: In a statement of charged expenditure, a clerk proposes to show the salaries and allowances of the Speaker and the Deputy Speaker of the Lok Sabha as voted expenditure. These salaries and allowances are in fact:

options.A: Met out of the Public Account of India
options.B: Charged on the Consolidated Fund of India
options.C: Submitted to the vote of the Lok Sabha every year
options.D: Paid out of the Contingency Fund of India

e: Article 97 provides that the salaries and allowances of the Speaker and Deputy Speaker of the Lok Sabha are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India, so they are shown as charged, not voted, expenditure.

q: During a financial year, the first batch of Supplementary Demands for Grants is ordinarily presented to Parliament in the:

options.A: Budget Session
options.B: Monsoon Session
options.C: Winter Session
options.D: Special Session

e: Supplementary Demands for Grants are ordinarily presented in three batches; the first batch is normally taken up in the Monsoon Session, the second in the Winter Session and the third in the Budget Session.

q:
Consider the following statements about the Public Accounts Committee of Parliament:
1. The Committee consists of twenty-two members, fifteen elected from the Lok Sabha and seven from the Rajya Sabha.
2. By convention, since 1967, the Chairman of the Committee is a member of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: The Public Accounts Committee has 22 members, 15 from the Lok Sabha and 7 from the Rajya Sabha, and by convention since 1967 its Chairman is a member of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha.

q:
Consider the following statements about the Departmentally Related Standing Committee on Railways:
1. The Committee consists of thirty-one members — twenty-one drawn from the Lok Sabha and ten from the Rajya Sabha.
2. The recommendations contained in the report of the Committee are binding, and a Demand for Grant cannot be voted until the report has been accepted by the Government.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: The Standing Committee on Railways has 31 members, 21 from the Lok Sabha and 10 from the Rajya Sabha. Its report is only recommendatory, so statement 2, which makes it binding, is wrong.

q: A Member of Parliament wants a Budget document which gives a detailed analysis of the tax revenues, the non-tax revenues and the capital receipts of the Government. The document he should refer to is the:

options.A: Expenditure Profile
options.B: Receipts Budget
options.C: Key to Budget Documents
options.D: Outcome Budget

e: The Receipts Budget gives the detailed analysis of tax revenues, non-tax revenues and capital receipts of the Government, which is exactly the information the member is looking for.

q: The Budget document which mainly presents a snapshot, that is, a broad overview, of the pattern of the total expenditure of the Government, ministry-wise and scheme-wise, is the:

options.A: Expenditure Profile
options.B: Detailed Demands for Grants
options.C: Memorandum Explaining the Provisions in the Finance Bill
options.D: Budget at a Glance

e: The Expenditure Profile presents a broad snapshot and overview of the total expenditure pattern of the Government, ministry-wise and scheme-wise, unlike the detailed head-wise Demands for Grants.

q: At the commencement of a financial year, before the full Budget has been voted, the Lok Sabha grants a Vote on Account for the Government. The Vote on Account:

options.A: Authorises the Government to levy taxes for a part of the financial year
options.B: Covers the estimates of receipts as well as of expenditure
options.C: Authorises withdrawal of money from the Consolidated Fund of India for meeting expenditure for a part of the financial year, pending completion of the budgetary process; it does not deal with the taxation proposals
options.D: Is required only when a new Government is formed after a general election

e: A Vote on Account under Article 116 authorises withdrawal from the Consolidated Fund of India to meet expenditure for part of the year pending completion of the budget process; it does not cover taxation proposals.

q: The Finance Bill is introduced in the Lok Sabha immediately after the presentation of the Budget, but it is taken up for consideration and passing:

options.A: Before the general discussion on the Budget takes place
options.B: After the Appropriation Bill has been passed
options.C: Only after the close of the financial year
options.D: Along with the Vote on Account, before the Demands are discussed

e: The Finance Bill is introduced immediately after the Budget presentation, but it is considered and passed only after the Demands are voted and the Appropriation Bill is passed, so that taxation follows authorisation of expenditure.

q:
Consider the following statements about the discussion of the Budget in Parliament:
1. No discussion on the Budget takes place in Parliament on the day on which it is presented.
2. During the general discussion on the Budget which follows, no motion can be moved and no voting on the Demands for Grants takes place.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: By parliamentary practice no discussion takes place on the day the Budget is presented, and during the general discussion that follows no motion is moved and no Demand is put to vote.

q: The apportionment of the earnings of through traffic among the zonal railways, over which the traffic has passed, is carried out:

options.A: Every month, through the Traffic Book compiled in the Traffic Accounts Office
options.B: Once a year, at the time of closing of the annual accounts
options.C: Only at the time of preparation of the Budget Estimates
options.D: Half-yearly, through the Debt Head Report

e: Apportionment of through-traffic earnings among zonal railways is done every month through the Traffic Book compiled in the Traffic Accounts Office, on the basis of the traffic carried over each railway.

q: A clerk in the Traffic Accounts Office proposes to apportion the Sundry Other Earnings of the railway also among the zonal railways, along with the traffic earnings. Apportionment among the zonal railways is actually carried out in respect of:

options.A: Sundry Other Earnings only
options.B: Coaching earnings and Goods earnings
options.C: All earnings, including Sundry Other Earnings
options.D: Passenger earnings only

e: Only Coaching earnings and Goods earnings are apportioned among zonal railways; Sundry Other Earnings are retained by the railway that earns them and are not apportioned.

q: An old budget file of the pre-merger period shows the grants voted for the Railways being authorised for withdrawal from the Consolidated Fund of India. In that period, such authorisation was given through:

options.A: The general Appropriation Act of the Union
options.B: An executive order of the Railway Minister
options.C: The Finance Act
options.D: A separate Appropriation (Railways) Act

e: Before the merger of the Railway Budget, withdrawals for railways from the Consolidated Fund of India were authorised by a separate Appropriation (Railways) Act, distinct from the general Appropriation Act.

q: A railway servant covered under the old pension scheme retires, and the cash equivalent of the leave salary standing to his credit, by way of leave encashment on retirement, falls due for payment. In the railway accounts, this payment is debited to:

options.A: The State Railway Provident Fund
options.B: The Capital Fund
options.C: The Development Fund
options.D: The Railway Pension Fund

e: Cash equivalent of leave salary on retirement under the old pension scheme is a pensionary benefit and is therefore debited to the Railway Pension Fund, from which pensionary charges are met.

q: Under the Separation Convention of 1924, after paying the fixed dividend on the Capital-at-charge, the Railways were required to contribute to the General Revenues, out of their surplus profits, the proportion of:

options.A: One-half of the surplus profits
options.B: One-third of the surplus profits
options.C: One-fifth of the surplus profits
options.D: The whole of the surplus profits

e: Under the Separation Convention of 1924, after paying the fixed dividend on Capital-at-charge, the Railways had to contribute one-fifth of their surplus profits to General Revenues.

q: A Member of Parliament asks in which session the Medium-Term Expenditure Framework Statement under the FRBM Act is laid, the Budget Session having already ended. The Statement is presented:

options.A: In the Session of Parliament following the Budget Session
options.B: Along with the Annual Financial Statement in the Budget Session itself
options.C: Only once in five years
options.D: To the Rajya Sabha alone

e: Under the FRBM Act, the Medium-Term Expenditure Framework Statement is laid in the Session of Parliament following the session in which the Annual Financial Statement is presented, i.e. after the Budget Session.

q: During the voting on a Demand for Grant, a cut motion moved by a member is adopted (carried) by the Lok Sabha. The adoption of a cut motion amounts to:

options.A: A mere suggestion which the Government may ignore
options.B: An increase in the amount of the Demand
options.C: Automatic passing of the Appropriation Bill
options.D: A vote of censure against the Government, expressing disapproval of the policy underlying the Demand

e: A cut motion is moved to express disapproval of the policy underlying a Demand; if it is adopted by the Lok Sabha it amounts to a vote of censure against the Government.

q: Two Bills connected with the Budget, one dealing with taxation along with other matters and the other dealing exclusively with the matters in Article 110, are sometimes confused with each other. Which of the following correctly distinguishes a 'Financial Bill' from a 'Money Bill'?

options.A: A Financial Bill can be introduced in either House of Parliament, whereas a Money Bill can be introduced only in the Rajya Sabha
options.B: A Financial Bill deals only with the matters enumerated in Article 110, whereas a Money Bill deals with taxation as well as other matters
options.C: A Money Bill deals exclusively with the matters enumerated in Article 110, whereas a Financial Bill contains some of those matters along with other matters and, after introduction in the Lok Sabha, is passed broadly like an ordinary Bill
options.D: A Financial Bill requires the prior recommendation of the President, whereas a Money Bill does not

e: A Money Bill deals exclusively with the matters in Article 110, whereas a Financial Bill contains some Article 110 matters along with other matters and, after introduction in the Lok Sabha, is passed broadly like an ordinary Bill.

q: The Committee on Public Undertakings of Parliament, which examines the reports and accounts of the public undertakings, consists of:

options.A: 15 members, all from the Lok Sabha
options.B: 22 members — fifteen drawn from the Lok Sabha and seven from the Rajya Sabha
options.C: 30 members, all from the Lok Sabha
options.D: 31 members — twenty-one from the Lok Sabha and ten from the Rajya Sabha

e: The Committee on Public Undertakings consists of 22 members, 15 drawn from the Lok Sabha and 7 from the Rajya Sabha, elected by the two Houses.

q: At the time of the presentation of the annual Budget, a number of documents are laid before Parliament by the Finance Minister. Which of the following is NOT among the documents presented along with the Budget?

options.A: The Annual Financial Statement
options.B: The Demands for Grants
options.C: The Finance Bill
options.D: The Appropriation Accounts

e: The Annual Financial Statement, Demands for Grants and the Finance Bill are presented with the Budget; the Appropriation Accounts are an after-the-year account document and are not a Budget document.

q: In the Seventh Schedule to the Constitution, 'Railways' is a subject in the Union List under Entry:
e: In the Seventh Schedule, Railways is Entry 22 of the Union List, placing it exclusively within the legislative competence of the Union.

q: A newly posted officer asks under which enactment the Railway Board, exercising the powers of the Central Government in respect of the Government Railways, was set up. The Board was set up under:

options.A: The Indian Railways Act, 1890
options.B: The Indian Railway Board Act, 1905
options.C: The Separation Convention of 1924
options.D: The Railways Act, 1989

e: The Railway Board was set up under the Indian Railway Board Act, 1905, to exercise the powers of the Central Government in respect of Government Railways.

q: An urgent requirement arises on the Railways for which an advance has to be taken pending authorisation by Parliament. For meeting such urgent and unforeseen expenditure, the Railways obtain advances from:

options.A: The Contingency Fund of India, there being no separate Contingency Fund for the Railways
options.B: A separate Railway Contingency Fund maintained by the Railway Board
options.C: The Depreciation Reserve Fund
options.D: The Railway Safety Fund

e: The Railways have no separate Contingency Fund; urgent and unforeseen expenditure pending Parliamentary authorisation is met by advances from the Contingency Fund of India under Article 267.

q: After a bill has been paid by a zonal railway, the voucher in support of the payment is stamped 'Paid' and cancelled. This is done primarily in order to:

options.A: Enable the voucher to be destroyed immediately after payment
options.B: Help the Cash & Pay Office in preparing the Cash Book
options.C: Indicate that the voucher has been checked by Audit
options.D: Prevent the same voucher from being presented again in support of another claim for payment

e: Stamping a paid voucher as Paid and cancelling it prevents the same voucher from being presented again in support of another claim and thus guards against double payment.

q: Two annual statements of the Railways, one presenting the year's receipts and disbursements in the Government form and the other exhibiting its assets and liabilities, are sometimes confused with each other. Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Finance Accounts of the Railways from their Balance Sheet?

options.A: The Finance Accounts are prepared by the zonal railways, whereas the Balance Sheet is prepared by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.B: The Finance Accounts present the receipts and disbursements of the year under the Major Heads of account in the Government form, whereas the Balance Sheet is a statement of the assets and liabilities of the Railways, including the Block Account and the balances of the Railway Funds
options.C: The Finance Accounts relate to capital transactions only, whereas the Balance Sheet relates to revenue transactions only
options.D: The Finance Accounts are presented to Parliament, whereas the Balance Sheet is never disclosed outside the Railway Board

e: The Finance Accounts present the year's receipts and disbursements under the Major Heads in Government form, whereas the Balance Sheet states the assets and liabilities, including the Block Account and Railway Fund balances.

q: In a pre-merger Railway Budget document, a clerk comes across Demand No. 15 in the list of Demands for Grants and has to identify the service it covered. Demand No. 15 of the erstwhile separate Railway Budget related to:

options.A: Appropriations to the Depreciation Reserve Fund
options.B: Open Line Works - Capital
options.C: Miscellaneous Expenditure (General)
options.D: Open Line Works - Revenue

e: In the erstwhile separate Railway Budget, Demand No. 15 related to Open Line Works - Revenue, covering revenue works on the open line.

q: During the course of a year, it is found that the amount of a grant sanctioned by Parliament for the Railways has to be increased. Such an increase in the amount of the grant can be effected only by:

options.A: An order of the Railway Board issued with the concurrence of the Financial Commissioner
options.B: A Supplementary Grant voted by Parliament
options.C: Re-appropriation of savings available under another grant
options.D: An order of the Ministry of Finance issued under the General Financial Rules

e: A sanctioned grant can be increased only by a Supplementary Grant voted by Parliament under Article 115; neither re-appropriation nor an executive order can increase the total grant.

q: The Estimates Committee of Parliament, while examining the estimates of a Ministry, does NOT go into:

options.A: The economies that can be effected in the implementation of the estimates
options.B: The merits of the policy underlying the estimates, the policy itself being a matter for Parliament
options.C: The organisation and efficiency of the Ministry
options.D: The form in which the estimates are presented to Parliament

e: The Estimates Committee examines economies, organisation, efficiency and the form of estimates, but it does not go into the merits of the policy underlying the estimates, policy being a matter for Parliament itself.

q: The Committee on Public Undertakings of Parliament, which examines the reports and accounts of the public undertakings on the basis of the audit reports of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India, was first constituted in the year:
e: The Committee on Public Undertakings was first constituted in 1964, on the recommendation of the Krishna Menon Committee, to examine public undertakings on the basis of CAG audit reports.

q: The members of the Public Accounts Committee of Parliament are chosen by the two Houses:

options.A: By nomination by the Speaker and the Chairman respectively
options.B: By election by a simple majority vote in each House
options.C: By nomination by the Finance Minister
options.D: By election in accordance with the system of proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote

e: Members of the Public Accounts Committee are elected by each House in accordance with the system of proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote.

q: In relation to the Public Accounts Committee of Parliament, the Comptroller and Auditor General of India is often described as the Committee's:

options.A: Chairman and convenor
options.B: Friend, philosopher and guide
options.C: Accounting authority
options.D: Executive agent

e: The CAG assists the Public Accounts Committee with audit reports and expert advice and is conventionally described as the Committee's friend, philosopher and guide.

q: The Departmentally Related Standing Committees of Parliament, which examine the Demands for Grants of the Ministries before they are voted, were set up in the year:
e: The Departmentally Related Standing Committees, which examine the Demands for Grants of Ministries before voting, were set up in 1993.

q: For the first weeks of a financial year after the merger, a zonal railway needs authority to spend before the Demands for Grants are voted. Since the merger of the Railway Budget with the Union Budget, such expenditure of the Railways for the initial part of the year is authorised through:

options.A: A separate Vote on Account taken exclusively for the Railways
options.B: The Railway Board's own budget orders
options.C: The common Vote on Account granted for the Government of India as a whole
options.D: Advances from the Depreciation Reserve Fund

e: Since the merger of the Railway Budget with the Union Budget, railway expenditure for the initial part of the year is covered by the common Vote on Account granted for the Government of India as a whole.

q: An imprest (permanent advance) is held by an officer of a zonal railway, who has not yet rendered an account of the expenditure incurred out of it. Until such an account is rendered, the imprest amount is treated in the accounts as:

options.A: Final expenditure of the railway
options.B: A deposit received from the officer
options.C: A part of the cash balance of the Cash & Pay Office
options.D: An advance outstanding against the holder

e: Until the holder renders an account of the expenditure, an imprest remains an advance outstanding against the holder in the accounts; it becomes final expenditure only on rendition and adjustment of the account.

q: A Bill pending in a House of Parliament would, if enacted, involve expenditure from the Consolidated Fund of India, and a doubt is raised whether it can be passed at all. Under Article 117(3) of the Constitution, such a Bill shall not be passed by either House of Parliament unless:

options.A: The President has recommended to that House the consideration of the Bill
options.B: The Speaker has certified that the Bill is a Financial Bill
options.C: The Finance Minister has concurred in the provisions of the Bill
options.D: The Bill has first been examined by the Estimates Committee

e: Article 117(3) bars either House from passing a Bill involving expenditure from the Consolidated Fund of India unless the President has recommended its consideration to that House.

q: After the Finance Commission submits its report, a question arises as to how its recommendations reach Parliament. The recommendations made by the Finance Commission under Article 280 of the Constitution are laid before each House of Parliament:

options.A: By the Finance Minister, along with the Demands for Grants
options.B: By the Chairman of the Finance Commission in person
options.C: By the Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.D: By the President, together with an explanatory memorandum as to the action taken thereon

e: Article 281 requires the President to cause the Finance Commission's recommendations to be laid before each House of Parliament together with an explanatory memorandum on the action taken thereon.

q: The Union Government proposes to make a grant to a State for a public purpose which does not fall within the legislative competence of the Union, and a doubt is raised about its permissibility. Under Article 282 of the Constitution, the Union or a State may make grants:

options.A: Only for purposes falling within its own legislative competence
options.B: Only for the purposes enumerated in the Union List or the State List, as the case may be
options.C: Only with the prior approval of the Finance Commission
options.D: For any public purpose, even if that purpose is not one with respect to which it may make laws

e: Article 282 expressly permits the Union or a State to make grants for any public purpose, even if that purpose is not one with respect to which it may make laws.

q: A member newly elected to the Public Accounts Committee of Parliament asks about the duration of his membership of the Committee. The members of the Committee hold office for a term of:

options.A: One year
options.B: Two years
options.C: Five years
options.D: The remaining term of the Lok Sabha

e: Members of the Public Accounts Committee hold office for a term of one year, the Committee being reconstituted annually.

q: The Chairman of the Public Accounts Committee of Parliament is:

options.A: Elected by the members of the Committee from amongst themselves
options.B: Nominated by the Finance Minister
options.C: Appointed by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha from amongst the Lok Sabha members of the Committee
options.D: The senior-most member of the Committee, by convention

e: The Chairman of the Public Accounts Committee is appointed by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha from amongst the Lok Sabha members of the Committee.

q: In the Union Budget, a clerk proposes to show the administrative expenses of the Election Commission of India as expenditure charged on the Consolidated Fund of India. These expenses are in fact:

options.A: Voted by Parliament, as part of the Demands for Grants of the Government
options.B: Charged on the Consolidated Fund of India
options.C: Met out of the Contingency Fund of India
options.D: Charged on the Public Account of India

e: The administrative expenses of the Election Commission are not in the charged list in Article 112(3); they are voted by Parliament as part of the Demands for Grants.

q: An Accounts Officer has to prepare the monthly Debt Head Report of the railway showing the balances under the debt, deposit, suspense and remittance heads. The Report is prepared from:

options.A: The station balance sheets rendered by the stations
options.B: The bank scrolls received from the accredited bank
options.C: The Works Registers maintained in the Accounts Office
options.D: The balances as recorded in the General Ledger (General Books) of the railway

e: The monthly Debt Head Report is prepared from the balances under debt, deposit, suspense and remittance heads as recorded in the General Ledger or General Books of the railway.

q: A zonal railway has already rendered its March (Preliminary) Account Current, and adjustments relating to the closing financial year are received thereafter. The March (Final) Account Current which follows serves mainly to:

options.A: Present the Budget Estimates of the following year to the Railway Board
options.B: Report the approximate earnings of the month of March
options.C: Incorporate the adjustments and corrections received after the rendering of the March (Preliminary) account, so that the accounts of the financial year are closed completely and correctly
options.D: Obtain the supplementary grant for the month of March

e: The March (Final) Account Current incorporates the adjustments and corrections received after the March (Preliminary) account, so that the accounts of the financial year are closed completely and correctly.

q: While explaining the principles of Government budgeting to a probationer, an officer refers to the principle of 'unity' (comprehensiveness). The principle requires that:

options.A: The estimates of expenditure are framed in gross terms, without netting off the related receipts
options.B: The authorisation of Parliament to incur expenditure is valid for one financial year only
options.C: All the receipts and expenditure of the Government are presented together in a single unified budget
options.D: The Budget of the Government is balanced every year

e: The principle of unity or comprehensiveness of budgeting requires that all receipts and expenditure of the Government are presented together in a single unified budget.

q: Every month, each station of a zonal railway renders a statement to the Traffic Accounts Office accounting for all its traffic transactions of the month and showing the balance due from the station. This monthly statement is known as the:

options.A: Station Balance Sheet
options.B: Traffic Book
options.C: Account Current
options.D: Cash Remittance Note

e: The monthly statement rendered by each station to the Traffic Accounts Office accounting for all its traffic transactions and showing the balance due from the station is the Station Balance Sheet.

q: A Station Master asks how frequently the earnings collected at his station must be remitted to the Cash Office or the accredited bank. The earnings are required to be remitted:

options.A: Once a week
options.B: Daily
options.C: Once a fortnight
options.D: At the end of the month

e: Station earnings must be remitted daily to the Cash Office or the accredited bank, so that cash collected does not accumulate at stations.

q: The Rashtriya Rail Sanraksha Kosh assures an annual outlay of Rs 20,000 crore for safety works, the major share being borne by Gross Budgetary Support. The amount of this assured annual outlay met from the internal resources of the Railways is:

options.A: Rs 10,000 crore
options.B: Rs 15,000 crore
options.C: Rs 20,000 crore
options.D: Rs 5,000 crore

e: Of the assured RRSK outlay of Rs 20,000 crore a year, Rs 15,000 crore is met from Gross Budgetary Support and the balance Rs 5,000 crore is met from the internal resources of the Railways.

q: A member of the Committee on Public Undertakings of Parliament asks who appoints the Chairman of that Committee. The Chairman is appointed by:

options.A: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
options.B: The President of India
options.C: The Finance Minister
options.D: The Chairman of the Rajya Sabha

e: The Chairman of the Committee on Public Undertakings is appointed by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha from amongst the members of the Committee.

q: A member elected to the Estimates Committee of Parliament in a particular year continues as a member of the Committee for a term of:

options.A: Five years
options.B: One year
options.C: Two years
options.D: The remaining term of the Lok Sabha

e: A member of the Estimates Committee holds office for a term of one year, the Committee being reconstituted annually, though members may be re-elected.
